audits.title: 627 Improving the Timing of Abdominal Ultrasonography for Women Presenting with Suspected Appendicitis: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.setting: Two hospitals, Lewisham and Greenwich Trust, London

cycle1.result: Average time from referral to ultrasound 14 hours 15 minutes.

audits.intervention: Posters of results in the surgical department.

cycle2.result: Average time from referral to ultrasound 4 hours 37 minutes.

audits.other_findings: A pathway allowing emergency doctors to request ultrasound is suggested.
audits.citation: Bastola D, Swafe L, Oke T. 627 Improving the Timing of Abdominal Ultrasonography for Women Presenting with Suspected Appendicitis: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.458.

audits.title: 640 Ambulatory Ultrasound - Could We Be More Efficient? Re-Audit -a District General Hospital Experience
audits.standard: National guidelines on ultrasound in selected patients with RIF pain
audits.setting: Ambulatory ultrasound, district general hospital (Royal Oldham Hospital)

cycle1.result: 41% had working diagnosis matching USS request; 13% had working diagnosis matched with USS results.

cycle2.result: 94 (86%) had working diagnosis matching USS request; 22 (20%) had working diagnosis matched with USS results.

audits.other_findings: USS reported no abnormality in 73 of 109; 101 patients discharged.
audits.citation: Idama D, Shafi A, Lasheen O, O'Connor A. 640 Ambulatory Ultrasound - Could We Be More Efficient? Re-Audit -a District General Hospital Experience. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.127.

audits.title: 550 A Closed Loop Audit of Ultrasound Use in Paediatric Patients Presenting with Abdominal Pain in a District General Hospital
audits.standard: Ultrasound as the recommended first-line imaging for suspected appendicitis in children
audits.setting: District general hospital, Mid Cheshire Hospitals, Crewe; patients up to age 16 admitted to general surgery

cycle1.result: Ultrasound used in 30% of patients diagnosed with appendicitis; MRI was the index modality in 42%.

audits.intervention: More ultrasound slots, access to sonographer training and a standardised ultrasound reporting format

cycle2.result: Ultrasound was the index imaging in 77%; specificity 93% (n=80), sensitivity 27% (n=11).

audits.other_findings: Only 5% of reports commented on all markers of inflammation; 25% needed re-imaging.
audits.citation: Pazvakavambwa H, Taaffe C, Otakoro O, Cheema A, Kazem M. 550 A Closed Loop Audit of Ultrasound Use in Paediatric Patients Presenting with Abdominal Pain in a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.563.

audits.title: TPTh 4.12 Utilisation of Risk Scoring and Imaging in Acute Appendicitis Diagnosis: A Retrospective Audit of Appendicitis Diagnostic Pathways
audits.standard: WSES (adults) and GIRFT (children) guidance: risk score all suspected appendicitis to guide imaging
audits.setting: District general hospital, Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: No adult had a risk score documented; 2 (9%) children had one; 9/46 (20%) imaged adults were low risk; 34/46 (74%) had CT first line.

audits.other_findings: 6/13 children who had ultrasound were high-risk males recommended for diagnostic laparoscopy without imaging.
audits.citation: Riad A, Akhtar Z, Ali M, Salerno G. TPTh 4.12 Utilisation of Risk Scoring and Imaging in Acute Appendicitis Diagnosis: A Retrospective Audit of Appendicitis Diagnostic Pathways. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.464.

audits.title: A QI Partnership to Decrease CT Use for Pediatric Appendicitis in the Community Hospital Setting.
audits.standard: Aim to reduce CT use by 50% (from 32% to 16%) in 1 year
audits.setting: Community general emergency department system, 3 institutions in Connecticut

cycle1.result: CT rate 32%; ultrasound rate 63%; nondiagnostic ultrasound 77%; transfer 23.5%.

audits.intervention: Paediatric appendicitis clinical pathway, ultrasound report templates, and case audit and feedback
audits.other_findings: Over-transfer rate was 0% at baseline; frontline staff reported knowledge gains and standardised practice.
audits.citation: Goldman MP, Lynders W, Crain M, Nocera Kelley M, Solomon DM, Bokhari SAJ, et al.. A QI Partnership to Decrease CT Use for Pediatric Appendicitis in the Community Hospital Setting. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2021;6(5):e479. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000479. PMID: 34589653.
